message.content:
Hydrogen (H) is the simplest and most abundant element in the universe. Here are its key properties:

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Common isotope** | Protium (^1H) – 99.98 % natural abundance |
| **Other stable isotopes** | Deuterium (^2H, D) – 0.02 %, Tritium (^3H) – radioactive, half‑life ≈12.32 yr |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.00794 u (average weighted by natural isotopic abundance) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Electron affinity** | –72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) at 1 atm |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) at 1 atm |
| **Density** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ at 25 °C, 1 atm |
| **Molar volume** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ (ideal gas at STP) |
| **State at room temperature** | Gas |
| **Bonding** | Forms covalent bonds; diatomic molecules (H₂) are the most common form |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; reacts with oxygen to form water (combustion) |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive as a reducing agent; forms hydrides with metals (e.g., NaH, CaH₂) |
| **Isotopic chemistry** | Deuterium and tritium used in nuclear fusion research (D-T fusion) |
| **Applications** | Fuel cells, rocket propellant (liquid hydrogen), industrial hydrogenation, semiconductor manufacturing, medical imaging (tritium labeling) |

These values are standard at 25 °C and 1 atm unless otherwise noted.
